thesis: URA is the largest and most liquid uranium/nuclear fuel-cycle ETF ($5.74B AUM, 0.69% expense ratio, 62 holdings, Cameco 21.81%). A clear dislocation has opened up: URA trades 36% below its 52-week high of $62.28 while spot U3O8 is ~$89.50/lb (up ~7% y/y) and the UxC long-term contract price hit an all-time high of ~$96/lb in August 2026, above the 2007 cycle peak. The drawdown is a de-rating of nuclear-adjacent equities — especially the pre-revenue reactor-developer sleeve (Oklo 5.75%, NuScale 2.92%) — not a deterioration in uranium fundamentals, where US utility contract coverage collapses from ~60% in 2030 to 9% by 2033. The main risk is that the speculative ~10% of the portfolio keeps compressing on its own: the fund's ~35x aggregate P/E carries equity-valuation risk independent of the uranium price.

base_case.assumptions: Spot holds $90–105/lb and the term price stays in the $95–100/lb range. Producer earnings catch up with record contract economics and URA reclaims its 200-day moving average of $48.30, while the pre-revenue developer holdings stay range-bound rather than re-rating. Implies roughly 15–35% upside from $40.13 over 18–36 months.

risks: Reactor-developer sleeve (Oklo, NuScale, X-energy, Lightbridge, NANO Nuclear) de-rates further — ~35x portfolio P/E is vulnerable independent of uranium
Spot drifts back to $70–80/lb as utility contracting stays paused, as it did in September 2026
